segments.say: The night has grown deep and soft. Somewhere across the city, the four friends Nadia had dinner with are asleep in their own homes, one by one. Tom has probably dreamed of teapots already. The group chat has gone quiet. The last laughing faces have been sent, and the phones have been put down on bedside tables in the dark.

Somewhere far away, the city carries on through the night. One by one, the lights in the windows go out. The restaurants are dark. The buses have stopped. The streets are empty and shining. Everyone who laughed today, everywhere, is gradually drifting into sleep, their faces soft, their breath slow.

And in a small house on a quiet street, Nadia has fallen asleep in her armchair, her blanket slipping a little from her knees. She's smiling slightly. Perhaps she's dreaming of a long wooden table, and four old friends, and a teapot lid in a sugar bowl. Whatever it is, it's a good dream. Let her rest. Let yourself rest too.

A window at night with the curtains half drawn, a low warm lamp on a small wooden table, a teapot and an empty cup, the street outside dark and still. It's the last picture of our evening. A small, warm room where a happy day has ended, and a long, peaceful night has begun.

If you'd like one last thought to carry with you, let it be a kind one. Your body has looked after you today in more ways than you could count. It has breathed and blinked and kept you warm. And every time you've laughed or smiled, today or any day, it was reaching out to someone, saying, I'm with you. You can trust it with this night.

For tonight, there are only three things, and you don't even need to try at them. Rest. Breathe. Let go. That's all. The rest will look after itself. The night is long and soft and kind. And you have all the time in the world to drift slowly, gently, all the way down into sleep.

Tomorrow will come, as it always does, and it will bring its own light, its own small tasks, and perhaps its own small laughs. But it isn't here yet. It's still far away, on the other side of a long, deep, restful night. You don't need to think about it now. It will wait for you, patiently, until you're ready.

There's no path to follow now. No street to walk down. No door to open. Just a soft darkness, warm and safe, and the faint, faraway quiet of a sleeping city. If your thoughts are becoming loose and strange, joining things that don't usually belong together, let them. That's only sleep, arriving quietly, by its own gentle road.

Stay here as long as you like. The bed is yours. The night is yours. There's nothing you need to wake for, and nothing you need to remember. Somewhere, very faintly, a lamp is still glowing in a window. Somewhere, an old friend is smiling in their sleep. And here, in this warm quiet room, you're resting, and that is more than enough.

One last time, notice your breath. In, slowly. And out, even more slowly. In. And out. There's nothing to add and nothing to change. Your body knows exactly how to do this, all night long, without any help from you. Just let it breathe you, gently, into sleep.

Notice the room around you, without opening your eyes if they're closed. The air is still. The walls are quiet. Whatever lies beyond them, the street, the city, the wide dark night, is far away now and doesn't need you. This small space is yours, warm and safe, and it will hold you gently until morning.

Tonight there's nothing to catch, no joke to keep up with, no conversation you need to follow. Nobody is waiting for you to answer or to laugh along. You can let your face be completely still, completely soft, the way it is only when we're alone and safe and drifting. It's a rare kind of rest. Let yourself have it.

show.sub: No laugh to keep up with

segments.say: Your body is heavier now than it was a moment ago. Your head is heavy on the pillow. Your arms are heavy at your sides. Your legs are heavy and still. Each breath out lets you sink a little further down, as if the bed were slowly, softly rising up to meet you. There's nowhere to go. Just down, gently, into rest.

Slower now. And slower. Softer. Quieter. Stiller. The words are almost finished. The voice is almost done. Let it fade into the quiet of the night, and let the quiet carry you down, gently, all the way into sleep.

So there's only one thing left to say. Thank you for spending this evening with Nadia and me, and for your curiosity. Be gentle with yourself, and laugh with the people you love whenever you can. Rest well, or sleep well. And the next time a laugh catches you by surprise, at a table, on a train or in a group chat, you can let it come, and remember this walk home.

Next time, we'll look at another small mystery of the human face, the sudden warm flush that rises in our cheeks when we're embarrassed, praised or caught out, and ask what researchers have found about why humans blush.
